reasoning.text: Reproducibility is high on the datapath math — the spec pins q, psi/omega/N^-1, Barrett mu/k, widths and parallelism so both impls converge on the same negacyclic NTT/INTT, and z3 confirms Barrett and the round-trip identity; the main reproducibility gap is everything structural (the actual conflict-free bank/offset functions, crossbar permutation, twiddle-ROM addressing, DIT/DIF convention and FSM), which each impl reconstructs differently. The biggest fidelity gap is that the paper's defining contribution — the conflict-free memory mapping — is both unspecified and, as supplied, provably non-conflict-free, and the quantified radix-4 op/area savings can't be exhibited by a behavioral model; parameters match the reference almost exactly, but the architecture reproduced is a generic correct NTT rather than CFNTT's scheme.
gaps: [control] The paper's actual conflict-free bank-index and offset functions (Sec. III headline result); supplied b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8 is provably NOT conflict-free for radix-2 strides 64/128/256/512
[control] Crossbar per-stage permutation sigma_s mapping logical operand indices to physical bank/lane ports
[operation] Twiddle-ROM address function f(stage s, block index) and negacyclic low/high-half storage layout
[operation] Decimation convention (DIT vs DIF) and global butterfly/stage ordering
[operation] Radix-4 fusion mapping: which two radix-2 stages fuse into each radix-4 BU, and the j-rotator sign convention
[timing] FSM states/transitions and per-stage cycle counts of the rearranged twiddle-stationary schedule
[operation] Modular adder/subtractor internal reduction policy (conditional ±q correction count)
[param] Primitive-root generator g (both picked g=11) and full twiddle-factor table contents
